ATT&CK publishes its techniques and sub-techniques as STIX attack-pattern objects, keeping their STIX ids. A STIX attack pattern may come from elsewhere, e.g. CAPEC, so the ATT&CK technique is the narrower.

ATT&CK publishes its mitigations as STIX course-of-action objects. A STIX course of action may be any action taken to prevent or respond to an attack, e.g. blocking a campaign's infrastructure, so the ATT&CK mitigation is the narrower.

D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise techniques and sub-techniques as offensive technique classes, named by their ATT&CK ids. D3FEND's offensive techniques also include classes of its own grouping them by tactic, e.g. Initial Access Technique, and ATT&CK's Mobile and ICS techniques are other D3FEND classes.

D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise tactics as offensive tactic classes, named by their ATT&CK ids, e.g. TA0001; the ATT&CK id is in the class IRI, not a property of its own, so the name joins them.
A property attack:Tactic and d3fend:OffensiveTactic share.

D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise mitigations, named by their ATT&CK ids, e.g. M1021, and relates each to the defensive techniques that implement it. ATT&CK's Mobile and ICS mitigations have no D3FEND counterpart, so the D3FEND class is the narrower.
A property attack:Mitigation and d3fend:ATTACKEnterpriseMitigation share.

A STIX file is one observed file, with its name and hashes; a D3FEND file is a class of digital artifact, e.g. Executable File or Email Attachment, that offensive techniques produce and defensive techniques analyse. An observed file is an instance of the classes it belongs to.
A STIX email message is one observed message; D3FEND's Email is a class of digital artifact, and D3FEND's email filtering and analysis techniques act on its instances.
A STIX URL is one observed URL; D3FEND's URL is a class of digital artifact, analysed by URL Analysis.
A STIX process is one observed process; D3FEND's Process is a class of digital artifact.
A STIX network traffic object is one observed flow; D3FEND's network traffic classes, e.g. Outbound Internet Web Traffic, are the kinds of traffic its filtering and analysis techniques act on.
